expectations.text: Corrects the premise: the GIL is NOT gone in the default Python 3.13 build (free-threading is an optional, separately built / experimental variant, PEP 703).
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Python 3.13 did not remove the GIL. It introduced experimental, opt-in support for a free-threaded build (via PEP 703) that can run with the GIL disabled, but this build is not the default" and "It added an experimental, opt-in free-threaded build (python3.13t) that is not the default." | grader 2: "Standard Python 3.13 keeps the GIL. The free-threaded build is separate and experimental... Python 3.13 did not remove the GIL. It added an experimental, opt-in free-threaded build (python3.13t) that is not the default."

expectations.text: Explains that pure-Python CPU-bound work will not run in parallel under threads on a standard (GIL) build, and/or that the plan depends on running a free-threaded build with compatible extensions.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "On the standard 3.13 build, threads do not run CPU-bound Python code in parallel. In a test on 3.13.3, 2 and 4 threads running the same loop took 1.31x and 1.60x longer in total than one thread." Also notes the free-threaded build "turns the GIL back on when it imports a C extension not marked as supporting free threading." | grader 2: "On the standard 3.13 build, threads do not run CPU-bound Python code in parallel. In a test on 3.13.3, 2 and 4 threads running the same loop took 1.31x and 1.60x longer in total than one thread."

expectations.text: Considers the imaging library: e.g. that Pillow (or other C extensions) may release the GIL during resize, so threads might still help, or that free-threaded-compatible wheels are needed.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Pillow already releases the GIL inside its C resample loops, so threads can run it in parallel on the standard build." and "If threads scale poorly, the library is holding the GIL. Stay on the tuned pool." Also flags that the production imaging library is unknown and may include GIL-holding steps (colour management, EXIF, custom filters). | grader 2: "Pillow already releases the GIL inside its C resample loops, so threads can run it in parallel on the standard build... For Pillow 11.3 on standard 3.13.3, two analysts measured: 8 threads: 10.6 s at 434 MB, against a spawned Pool(8) at 10.5 s and about 830 MB."

expectations.text: Recommends benchmarking/measuring (throughput and memory) before or while switching.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Run an A/B test on production images: ThreadPoolExecutor(N) against Pool(N), measuring wall time and peak PSS." and "Measure per-worker PSS and split it into idle overhead versus in-flight buffers before choosing between tuning and threads." | grader 2: "Run an A/B test on production images: ThreadPoolExecutor(N) against Pool(N), measuring wall time and peak PSS." and "do first (verified): Before any thread-based design, run a thread-versus-pool benchmark on the production interpreter, imaging library and real images."

expectations.text: Gives a clear verdict on the plan as stated (e.g. "not for the reason you gave" / "not as stated" / "only if ..."), not an unresolved "it depends".
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Council verdict: Partly. Keep multiprocessing.Pool and tune it for memory first. Switch to threads only after a benchmark on your real library proves it, because Python 3.13 did not remove the GIL." and option 4 rated "partly sound. The stated reason is false: 3.13 did not remove the GIL. The move can still work on the standard build if the library does its heavy work in C with the GIL released." The verdict is conditional but concrete (tune now, switch only if benchmark passes), and the 'Confidence: low' label somewhat softens it, though the action sequence remains explicit. | grader 2: "Council verdict: Partly. Keep multiprocessing.Pool and tune it for memory first. Switch to threads only after a benchmark on your real library proves it, because Python 3.13 did not remove the GIL." — a concrete top-line recommendation with a stated condition, not a bare 'it depends'.

factual_errors: Minor: "a 3000x3000 RGB image is about 27 MB decoded" and "4000x3000 is about 36 MB" use 3 bytes/pixel; Pillow stores RGB internally at 4 bytes/pixel (RGBX), so the actual decoded buffers are ~36 MB and ~48 MB respectively. The raw-RGB arithmetic is correct, but as a Pillow memory estimate it is low by a third. (The separately quoted ~48 MB measurement for 3000x3000 is consistent with the 4-byte layout.)
